mechanism_narrative: A sustained collapse in TRANSIT mobility below -30 percent signals a broad withdrawal from out-of-home routines that mechanically reduces retail footfall, keeping RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: TRANSIT fell from 0.6 at t-3w to -70.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is greater than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days while TRANSIT remains below -30 percent.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES mobility drops more than 20 percentage points week-on-week, commuting-driven retail demand falls sharply, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 20 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES fell from -19.9 at t-1w to -48.9 at t-0w, a 29-point drop
failure_condition: After a week-on-week WORKPLACES drop greater than 20 points, RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of RESIDENTIAL mobility above +10 and PARKS mobility below -10 indicates widespread stay-at-home behavior, which suppresses discretionary retail trips and drives RETAIL_REC down over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact: RESIDENTIAL = 23.6 and PARKS = -51.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: When RESIDENTIAL > 10 and PARKS < -10 simultaneously, RETAIL_REC increases over the next 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: The extreme one-week drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES at t-0w is a transient shock; as these series stabilize and partially recover from their troughs, retail footfall rebounds, making the next four-week mean RETAIL_REC higher than the last four-week mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each improve by at least 10 points from t-0w within two weeks
evidence_refs: fact: both series hit their lowest values at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve by at least 10 points from t-0w within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility below -20 percent signals reduced essential shopping trips and a broader consumer retrenchment that spills over into retail-and-recreation, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: GROCERY_PHARM fell to -26.7 at t-0w from -4.3 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM falls below -20 percent.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, a fall in RESIDENTIAL mobility below +10 indicates a return to out-of-home activity, which increases retail-and-recreation visits and drives RETAIL_REC up over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: RESIDENTIAL is currently 23.6, a stay-at-home level
failure_condition: In a reopening regime, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days fails to rise when RESIDENTIAL falls below +10.

mechanism_narrative: Seasonal spring weather increases PARKS mobility, and higher PARKS activity is a leading indicator of broader outdoor-oriented consumer traffic that lifts RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: PARKS was +17.9 at t-3w before falling to -51.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not increase when PARKS mobility rises from its current level.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous condition of TRANSIT below -40 and WORKPLACES below -40 identifies a severe mobility suppression regime; retail footfall collapses further because both commuting and discretionary travel are curtailed, so RETAIL_REC falls over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact: TRANSIT = -70.9 and WORKPLACES = -48.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: When TRANSIT < -40 and WORKPLACES < -40 simultaneously, RETAIL_REC increases over the next 7 days.
